rule: After each code/debug slice, read this file, inspect the current project state, identify real errors and shortcomings, fix what is safely in scope, and record remaining gaps as explicit findings.
hard_constraints: do not stage commit or push
do not treat roadmap items as implemented
do not claim completion from a narrow check
required_checks: run the touched demo or compiler path
search active FASM/sample paths for forbidden syntax drift
record at least one real project issue or shortcoming

findings.evidence: A newly created docs/polyglot_fasm_snapsurf_deep_analysis.md conflicted with the active no-.md rule.
findings.fix: Moved report content into docs/polyglot_fasm_snapsurf_deep_analysis.jsonl and deleted the .md artifact.

findings.evidence: The wrapper previously verified only one large vector length, so len 0..3 and tail boundaries were not directly tested.
findings.fix: Added verify_boundary_lengths for lengths 0..17 across pointer offsets 0..2.

findings.evidence: run.sh checked x86_64 but not Linux, while Prompt requires Linux x86_64.
Prompt.jsonl describes a complete systems language; current SnapSurf remains a verified FASM foundation subset.
findings.next: Implement broad language features only as future bounded slices with tests.

findings.evidence: Prompt asks for official doc chapter/line citations; no vendored stable-line official PDFs exist in the repo.
findings.next: Vendor exact reference docs or cite stable document sections without inventing line numbers.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl requires arithmetic and bitwise operators, but `xor` was tokenized as an identifier and `./build/surf build tests/pass/bitwise_xor` failed before this slice.
findings.fix: Added TOK_XOR, AST_BIN_XOR, keyword parsing, precedence, type checking, debug names, colorization, runtime FASM emission, constant folding, and a regression fixture that emits `xor rax, rcx`.

findings.evidence: Direct `./build/surf build tests/pass/bitwise_xor` failed inside the sandbox at FASM assembly, while escalated execution of the same command succeeded.
findings.next: Keep recording when commands require unsandboxed FASM process execution instead of treating E1001 as a compiler regression without confirming.

findings.evidence: This slice only implements integer `xor`; integer shifts, bitwise-not, and separate integer `and`/`or` semantics are still not implemented.
findings.next: Add each remaining bitwise operator as its own failing fixture, parser/type/emitter change, and full-regression pass.

findings.evidence: Initial tests/pass/bitwise_shl and tests/pass/bitwise_shr fixtures stopped at E0903 because their surf.pkg files only contained `package <name>` and missed version/type/target/runtime/entry/requires/end fields.
findings.fix: Updated both surf.pkg files to match existing executable fixture schema before using them as compiler evidence.

findings.evidence: After fixture repair, `shl` and `shr` tokenized as TokIdent and dump-ast failed with E0404 function not found, proving the active compiler did not parse shifts as operators.
findings.fix: Added TOK_SHL/TOK_SHR, AST_BIN_SHL/AST_BIN_SHR, keyword parsing, Pratt precedence, integer type checking, token/AST debug names, colorization, runtime FASM `shl rax, cl` and `shr rax, cl` emission, constant folding, and regression fixtures returning 16 and 10.

findings.evidence: The current implementation follows x86-64 CL-count masking semantics for runtime and constant folding, but the language spec does not yet define explicit invalid/large shift-count behavior.
findings.next: Define SnapSurf shift-count semantics before broad integer-width expansion.

findings.evidence: Integer bitwise-not and distinct integer `and`/`or` semantics are still not implemented; current `and`/`or` remain boolean operators.
findings.next: Implement each remaining bitwise operator as a separate failing fixture and verified compiler slice.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/bitwise_and` and `./build/surf build tests/pass/bitwise_or` failed with E0501 because semantic_expr forced AST_BIN_AND and AST_BIN_OR through bool-only type checking.
findings.fix: Added a bool-or-integer semantic path for AST_BIN_AND and AST_BIN_OR: bool operands still return bool, while matching integer operands now return the integer type and use the existing FASM `and rax, rcx` and `or rax, rcx` runtime templates.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl requires bitwise NOT, but this slice only fixed integer `and` and `or`; there is still no verified integer bitwise-not token/AST/emitter fixture.
findings.next: Implement bitwise-not as a separate failing fixture and compiler slice.

findings.evidence: The same `and` and `or` spellings now serve bool logic and integer bitwise operations, with type-selected semantics; the current emitter evaluates both operands and does not implement short-circuit boolean control flow.
findings.next: Define whether SnapSurf wants strict boolean operators, short-circuit logical operators, or separate bitwise spellings before side-effect-sensitive boolean expressions are expanded.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/bitwise_not` and `./build/surf build tests/pass/bitwise_not` failed with E0501 because AST_UNARY_NOT only accepted bool operands.
findings.fix: Kept the existing `not` token and AST_UNARY_NOT, changed semantic checking to accept bool or matching integer operands, emitted logical-not for bool and FASM `not rax` for integer operands, and added tests/pass/bitwise_not returning exit 15.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl lists rotate left/right under bitwise operations, but active compiler still has no verified `rol` or `ror` token, AST node, type check, emitter template, or regression fixture.
findings.next: Implement rotate left/right as a separate bounded compiler slice with failing fixtures first.

findings.evidence: Integer bitwise-not currently emits `not rax`; the language has not defined whether i32/u32 results must be masked to declared width before return, storage, comparison, or future wider integer lowering.
findings.next: Define integer-width and truncation semantics before claiming precise fixed-width bitwise behavior beyond current executable exit-code evidence.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `rol` and `ror` tokenized as TokIdent and `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/bitwise_rol` plus `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/bitwise_ror` failed with E0404 function not found.
findings.fix: Added TOK_ROL/TOK_ROR, AST_BIN_ROL/AST_BIN_ROR, keyword parsing, Pratt precedence, integer type checking, token/AST debug names, colorization, runtime FASM `rol rax, cl` and `ror rax, cl` emission, constant folding, and regression fixtures returning 1 and 16.

findings.evidence: Rotate runtime emission and constant folding follow x86-64 CL-count masking and 64-bit RAX behavior, while Prompt.jsonl expects fixed-width systems-language integer semantics that are not yet formally defined in the active compiler subset.
findings.next: Define SnapSurf rotate-count and fixed-width truncation rules before claiming exact i32/u32 rotate semantics beyond current executable evidence.

findings.evidence: The verified bitwise surface is now broader, but Prompt.jsonl describes a complete systems language; generics, ownership, modules, richer diagnostics, and many ABI/runtime features remain outside this bounded FASM foundation slice.
findings.next: Continue with one failing fixture and one verified compiler slice per feature instead of marking the full Prompt complete.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl requires exponentiation, but before this slice `pow` tokenized as TokIdent and `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/arithmetic_pow` plus `./build/surf build tests/pass/arithmetic_pow` failed with E0404 function not found.
findings.fix: Added TOK_POW, AST_BIN_POW, keyword parsing, Pratt precedence above multiplication, integer type checking, token/AST debug names, colorization, runtime FASM loop emission using `imul rax, rcx`, constant folding, and tests/pass/arithmetic_pow returning exit 32.

findings.evidence: Runtime and constant folding currently return 1 for non-positive exponents and inherit unchecked 64-bit multiply overflow, while Prompt.jsonl requires defined overflow behavior and a full arithmetic policy.
findings.next: Define negative exponent, zero exponent, overflow, and fixed-width truncation semantics before claiming complete integer exponentiation.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl also lists pow, sqrt, cbrt, trig, logs, GCD/LCM, and bitcount operations in the standard library; this slice only adds the integer `pow` operator spelling used by the active compiler subset.
findings.next: Add standard-library math functions only as separate fixtures and verified compiler/runtime support.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl requires pointer-sized integer type `usize`, and TYPE_ISIZE/TYPE_USIZE plus integer predicates already existed, but before this slice `usize` and `isize` were tokenized as TokIdent and `./build/surf dump-ast tests/pass/primitive_pointer_sized` failed with E0404 unsupported token.
findings.fix: Added length-5 parsing for `isize` and `usize` in parse_type_keyword, added tests/pass/primitive_pointer_sized covering declaration, arithmetic, equality, boolean conjunction, build, runtime exit 0, and full-regression.

findings.evidence: The first primitive_pointer_sized fixture parsed after the type fix but failed semantic checking because `bytes == 40` compared `usize` with the default integer literal type instead of using a typed expected value.
findings.next: Define integer literal coercion/range checking for typed contexts and comparisons before claiming ergonomic fixed-width integer semantics.

findings.evidence: `isize` and `usize` currently lower through the existing 64-bit RAX expression path on x86_64; the language has not yet documented cross-target pointer-width behavior or truncation/range rules.
findings.next: Specify pointer-sized integer width, overflow, and cross-target lowering rules before adding non-x86_64 backends.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl requires coercion rules, and before this slice `./build/surf check tests/pass/typed_int_literal_compare` failed with E0501/E0403 because comparisons such as `words == 40` and `12 == delta` typed literals as default i32 instead of the known integer operand type.
findings.fix: Changed comparison type checking to pass the left integer type as expected type for right-side literals and to retype a left-side integer literal against the right operand's integer type, then added tests/pass/typed_int_literal_compare to full-regression.

findings.evidence: The literal coercion path now assigns the contextual integer type but still does not validate whether the literal value fits i8/u8/i16/u16/etc.; this is required before claiming complete fixed-width integer semantics.
findings.next: Add literal value extraction plus signed/unsigned range diagnostics for typed contexts and comparisons.

findings.evidence: This slice covers integer comparison operands and existing declaration/return expected-type paths; function call arguments and broader implicit conversion policy are not fully specified.
findings.next: Define a language-wide coercion matrix before expanding coercions beyond integer literals.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `./build/surf check tests/compile_fail/integer_literal_range` accepted `let small u8 = 256` with `check ok`; after the semantic range check it fails at the literal with E0501 and full-regression covers the compile-fail case.
findings.fix: Added semantic_int_literal_fits_type for contextual AST_INT_LIT checks across i8/u8/i16/u16/i32/u32/i64/isize and a pass fixture for boundary values 127, 255, 32767, and 65535.

findings.evidence: Unary negative expressions still flow through the existing unary_i32 path, so smaller signed typed negative literals are not yet treated as target-typed integer literals with range checks.
findings.next: Teach AST_UNARY_NEG over integer literals to use expected_expr_type and validate signed lower bounds before claiming complete signed literal coercion.

findings.evidence: The lexer builds TOK_INT payloads by multiplying and adding into a qword without overflow detection; the new semantic helper can check narrower target ranges but cannot reject decimal literals that overflow while tokenizing for u64/usize.
findings.next: Add lexer-level integer overflow detection or preserve literal text for checked parsing before claiming full u64/usize literal safety.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `./build/surf check tests/pass/negative_integer_literals` rejected `let min8 i8 = -128` with E0501 because AST_UNARY_NEG flowed through the i32-only semantic path; after the fix the fixture checks, builds, exits 0, and full-regression includes it.
findings.fix: Added target-typed unary negative integer semantic handling, signed lower-bound checks for i8/i16/i32/i64/isize, unsigned negative rejection through signed-type validation, and left-side `-literal` comparison retyping.

findings.evidence: tests/compile_fail/negative_integer_literal_range now rejects `let too_small i8 = -129` at the literal with E0501 and the expected output is covered by full-regression.
findings.fix: Added semantic_neg_int_literal_fits_type using the absolute signed lower-bound magnitude for each signed integer type.

findings.evidence: This slice still depends on the existing qword TOKEN_PAYLOAD; literals larger than u64 can wrap before semantic checks see the source magnitude.
findings.next: Add checked lexer parsing or source-span reparse for integer literals before claiming full numeric literal overflow diagnostics.

findings.evidence: The backend stores and compares integer values through the existing 64-bit RAX/local-slot path; i8/i16/i32 width truncation or sign-extension boundaries are still not formally enforced at every expression/storage boundary.
findings.next: Define and test integer width normalization before claiming complete fixed-width backend semantics.

findings.evidence: Before this slice, `./build/surf check tests/compile_fail/integer_literal_overflow` accepted `let too_big u64 = 18446744073709551616` with `check ok` because lexer integer payload accumulation wrapped in a qword.
findings.fix: Added lexer-level unsigned multiply/add overflow checks, diagnostic E0106, a compile-fail fixture for u64::MAX+1, and full-regression coverage.

findings.evidence: The new overflow diagnostic reports the source position at the start of the overflowing decimal literal, producing stable expected output at line 2 column 23.
findings.fix: The lexer preserves the literal start line/column in r10/r11 and uses those values when printing E0106.

findings.evidence: Even with lexer overflow fixed, the backend still stores and computes declared narrow integers through the existing 64-bit RAX/local-slot path; global truncation/sign-extension behavior is not fully specified.
findings.next: Define width-normalization rules and add fixtures for assignment, arithmetic, comparison, and return boundaries.

findings.evidence: Prompt.jsonl describes a broad systems language; this slice only hardens decimal integer literal parsing in the active FASM foundation compiler.
findings.next: Continue with one bounded failing fixture and one verified compiler slice per remaining feature.
